target.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check
target.body:
## Decision Requested

Should OpenClaw own a small set of named, release-tested hosting contracts and report whether the running process currently satisfies the selected contract?

This extends surfaces OpenClaw already owns: Gateway `/ready` and `/readyz`, health, and status. It does **not** add a second config system, a general policy engine, or a hosted-platform abstraction.

Readiness criteria and hosting profiles compose but are separable. A general runtime invariant can extend existing Gateway/default readiness without defining a profile. A new profile is only for a distinct, named support posture that selects a different composition of existing criteria.

## The Concrete Gap

OpenClaw can run in containers today, but "the process is alive" is not the same as "this runtime shape is usable."

For example, a container can start with a loopback-only Gateway. Existing lifecycle readiness may correctly say the process is healthy while the selected container topology is unreachable. Hosts currently close that gap with private startup scripts, baked config checks, and downstream-only readiness logic.

Profiles make the support promise executable:

```text
OpenClaw supports these runtime shapes.
Each shape has stable predicates and failure reasons.
Each release validates them.
A running instance reports which shape it selected and whether it satisfies it.
```

They also provide a supportable subset against which maintainers can reproduce hosted issues instead of debugging an unbounded combination of deployment settings.

## Evidence From Existing Issues

| Issue | What operators observe | What the contract needs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [openclaw#96084](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/96084) | `/readyz` remains healthy when a full PVC makes workspace writes fail. | A workspace-writable status fact and stable readiness condition. |
| [openclaw#78136](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78136) | Docker remains ready while the command queue is draining and rejects work. | Admission/drain state in required readiness. |
| [openclaw#73652](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/73652) | The Gateway accepts connections before internal startup is ready. | A truthful startup admission boundary. |
| [openclaw#78954](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78954) | Plugin/channel startup can block usable core Gateway startup. | Required versus advisory conditions. |
| [openclaw#43886](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/43886) | A Docker Gateway intended for LAN still listens on loopback. | Effective topology checks, not configured intent alone. |

These issues motivate reusable readiness criteria. They do not each require a new profile: generally applicable invariants extend existing/default readiness, while profiles compose criteria only when OpenClaw wants to name and release-test a distinct support posture. Related reports also ask for truthful service-manager readiness ([openclaw#66512](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/66512)) and channel health ([openclaw#101083](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101083)).

## Proposed Built-In Contracts

| Profile | Intended posture | Additional required readiness |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `local` | Default foreground/local runtime | Config loaded and Gateway observed |
| `container` | Gateway directly reachable through a container listener | Effective local Gateway listener is resolved and non-loopback |
| `reverse-proxy` | Gateway behind a trusted identity proxy | Trusted-proxy auth has a user header and at least one trusted source |
| `node-mode` | Gateway/controller for one or more execution nodes | An approved node is live, correlated, controllable, and advertises an allowed command |

A profile describes OpenClaw's ingress/runtime posture, not physical packaging. A Gateway running in Docker behind a trusted identity proxy selects `reverse-proxy`; a directly exposed Gateway selects `container`.

Selection is explicit but optional:

```text
openclaw gateway run --hosting-profile container
OPENCLAW_HOSTING_PROFILE=container
openclaw.json: hosting.profile
```

Precedence is startup flag, environment, config, then the `local` default. Selection validates the effective runtime; it does not generate or change configuration.

## Canonical Readiness Result

Each condition carries:

```text
type + status + requirement + reason + message
```

| Class | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `required` | `False` or `Unknown` blocks readiness and appears in `failures` |
| `advisory` | `False` or `Unknown` appears in `advisories` but does not change HTTP 200 to 503 |

Existing Gateway startup, channel, drain, and event-loop failures remain authoritative and are merged into `failures`. The binary result stays suitable for Docker and Kubernetes while health/status retain degraded-state diagnostics.

The same top-level result is projected through `/ready`, `/readyz`, health, status summary, and `status --json`. Hosts do not need to choose among duplicate readiness representations.

## Normative Schemas

The RFC source now defines the closed `HostingProfileId` and strict `hosting.profile` config shape, the exact condition/result types, and transport projection rules. Detailed HTTP readiness flattens the canonical object once into the legacy Gateway envelope; Gateway health and `status --json` embed it once as `readiness`. It also defines required empty arrays, condition uniqueness by `type`, set semantics for failures/advisories, non-contractual ordering, stable reasons, non-normative messages, unauthenticated remote redaction, and the existing fail-closed internal-evaluation envelope.

## Boundaries And Compatibility

- No profile selection is required; existing installations resolve to `local`.
- Profiles use existing config and effective runtime facts. There is no parallel hosted config tree.
- Profiles never generate, merge, or repair config.
- Profile readiness is ANDed with existing Gateway readiness.
- Only required conditions affect binary readiness.
- Core owns only built-in predicates; policy, doctor, OCC, Lobster, and optional plugins are not dependencies.
- Docker/Kubernetes/systemd continue to own retries, intervals, start periods, and timeouts.
- Plugin activation diagnostics are advisory in `local`, preserving the HTTP behavior of existing healthy probes.
- Invalid explicit profile values fail rather than silently selecting another profile.

`managed` is deliberately deferred because it does not yet define an invariant distinct from `reverse-proxy`. Custom profiles and custom evidence publication are also deferred until a separate contract defines trust, identity, scoping, and freshness.

## Why Core Instead Of Doctor Or Policy?

Doctor can diagnose or repair static configuration. Policy can restrict allowed configuration. Both are optional.

Supervisors consume readiness during startup and continuously afterward. Core owns the authoritative live Gateway, plugin, proxy, pairing, and node-registry facts. Doctor and policy can consume the canonical result later without becoming startup dependencies.

## Smallest Useful Landing

1. Canonical condition shape plus default `local` projection on existing readiness, health, and status.
2. Explicit selection plus `container` and `reverse-proxy` predicates.
3. `node-mode` predicates from pairing and the live node registry.
4. Promote the packaged profile matrix into blocking package-acceptance release checks.

The first slice is independently useful. The readiness foundation can be accepted without committing to every proposed profile at once.

## Concrete Draft Stack

| Slice | Draft fork PR | Reviewed head |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local readiness surfaces | https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/17 | `cefbe89976` |
| Built-in profile selection and predicates | https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/18 | `c423b77720` |
| Node-mode readiness | https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/19 | `0dc6c7184f` |
| Release conformance gate | https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/21 | `504310c0b9` |

Each slice was tested and reviewed against its actual base. The three runtime slices build one package-installed Docker conformance lane, and the fourth promotes it into blocking release checks:

- PR 17 covers default `local`.
- PR 18 covers ready and invalid `container` and `reverse-proxy` postures.
- PR 19 covers `node-mode` transitioning from HTTP 503 to 200 after a real node host is paired and connected.
- PR 21 selects the matrix in non-advisory package acceptance and preserves the normal targeted Docker artifacts.

After the schema/projection audit, the final composed runtime stack passed 193 focused assertions, plus the release-workflow assertion, 33 Docker scenario-plan assertions, formatting, package-boundary, and diff checks. PR 21 also passes the exact release-workflow assertion, all 33 Docker planner assertions, selected-lane package/image planning, formatting, diff checks, and a full branch Codex review against PR 19 with no actionable findings. Brokered Linux execution remains pending because Crabbox stalled before allocating a lease; no remote runtime success is claimed.

## OCC And AgentHarness Alignment

OCC can select a profile as declarative desired state. OpenClaw evaluates it in the runtime plane. OCC remains responsible for desired state, identity, admission, restrictions, quotas, policy compilation, provisioning, and audit indexing; it does not enter channel, session, tool, approval, or AgentHarness traffic.

Lobster and other hosts remain responsible for auth integration, tenant routing, policy rollout, telemetry, administration, and deployment. OpenClaw owns only the generic workload contract those hosts should not reimplement.

target.title: RFC: Claws
target.body:
## Summary

- Defines one Claw package as one complete new OpenClaw agent for one job.
- Makes `claws add` create a new `agents.list[]` entry and workspace; existing agent/workspace collisions fail closed.
- Replaces flat `entries[]` with grouped `agent`, `workspace`, `packages`, `mcpServers`, and `cronJobs` ownership boundaries.
- Keeps skills, plugins, MCP servers, heartbeat, and Gateway cron on their existing OpenClaw owner surfaces.
- Uses enclosing `package.json` plus authenticated publishing for package identity/version/publisher ownership.
- Excludes models, providers, credentials, channel bindings, `agent.skills`, and generic connectors from the portable contract.
- Gates the entire draft CLI behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`; when disabled, the command is unregistered and absent from help/completions.

## Lifecycle

The proposed lifecycle is `add`, `status`, `update`, `remove`, and `export`. `add --dry-run --json` previews the complete agent, workspace, package, MCP, and cron action set. Every declared component is required; unsupported or blocked components fail the complete add.

## Implementation Status

The existing OpenClaw draft stack is prototype evidence for parsing, installers, SQLite provenance, file safety, MCP config, doctor, update, and export. It is not the accepted compatibility contract and must be restacked around the grouped schema and one-new-agent invariant before any implementation PR is made ready.

The RFC now defines reviewable implementation slices for schema/dry-run, agent creation, workspace files, skill/plugin packages, MCP, heartbeat/cron, status/doctor/remove, update, export, and ClawHub/feed publication.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- Manual consistency scan for stale public `claws apply`, flat-entry, optional-component, and connector semantics
- Review against Patrick Erichsen's requested product-model and schema boundaries
